newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA TAKES THIRD SLALOM VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA TAKES THIRD SLALOM VICTORY.

text.p: In-form Austrian Thomas Sykora continued his domination of the slalom and captured his third World Cup victory of the season at a men's race on Monday.
Sykora produced a stunning second run despite almost crashing out on numerous occasions, to clock a winning aggregate time of one minute 41.93 seconds.
The 28-year-old Austrian has now won three of the four slaloms staged this winter and finished second in the other, to take a commanding lead in the discipline's standings on 380 points.
Frenchman Sebastien Amiez, the defending slalom World Cup title-holder, was second on the Podkoren piste in 1:42.29 for his best result of the season.
Austria's 1994 Olympic slalom champion Thomas Stangassinger fell back to overall third in 1:42.34 after a first-descent lead in foggy and snowy conditions.
World champion Alberto Tomba disappointed the many Italian fans at the Slovenian resort with eighth place.
